newsitem.title: JAPAN: Matsushita says completes 64-bit game development.
newsitem.headline: Matsushita says completes 64-bit game development.

text.p: Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd said on Tuesday that it has developed a 64-bit game machine and more than 10 software titles to play on it.
A Matsushita spokesman said, however, that the company has not decided when to start selling the game system.

"We started development of the 64-bit game system last year and we have already finished development of the hardware. Also we have already finished developing more than 10 software titles, but the commercialisation of the system, originally scheduled for the end of 1996, has been delayed," the Matsushita spokesman said.

He denied a report published in the Japanese industrial daily Nihon Kogyo Shimbun on Tuesday that said Matsushita would stop developing a home-use 64-bit game machine and withdraw from the home-use game system business.
The paper also said Matsushita would liquidate the unit set up for its game business.
The newspaper said Matsushita made the decision because Sony, Nintendo Co Ltd and Sega Enterprises Ltd dominate the home-game market.
